By John Bromels – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:15AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Cipher Digital ›

When I first bought stock in Nvidia (NVDA -3.30%) in 2018, the advanced level of artificial intelligence (AI) we have now only existed on Dario Amodei's future plans spreadsheet. Back then, the thesis for owning Nvidia was all about crypto mining.

Nvidia's sales had skyrocketed in 2017 thanks to eager Bitcoin (BTC -3.21%) miners snapping up the company's graphics processing units (GPUs), which had proven to be the speediest, most powerful processors for crypto mining facilities.

Alas, that fervor didn't last. In 2018, the price of Bitcoin crashed, taking Nvidia's share price along with it. It wasn't until the advent of AI that the company's high-end processor chips suddenly found themselves in high demand again.

But now that Nvidia's stock has taken another hit, it's natural for AI investors to wonder if there are better bets for their money to grow.

Here are two under-the-radar AI stocks with far more room to 10x their share price than Nvidia. Like Nvidia, both are former stars of the Bitcoin mining era that are now bets on AI infrastructure. Unlike Nvidia, their market caps are measured in billions, not trillions, making them much more likely to 10x.

Nvidia makes the processor chips that perform the complex (and energy-intensive) calculations required by AI models and crypto mines alike. But by themselves, they're just tiny pieces of silicon. To work, Nvidia's chips need to be hooked up to massive servers that supply the memory, data, and communications infrastructure that the processors require.

That's where a company like Cipher Digital (CIFR -1.37%) comes in. Cipher started out as a Bitcoin miner, but is now building AI data centers and leasing their capacity to customers. Cipher Digital took advantage of Texas' industry-friendly regulatory environment to focus its operations there.

The company boasts 3.4 gigawatts (GW) of grid capacity across 11 data center sites "at various stages of interconnection," with enough onsite natural gas generation capacity to support 2.5 additional GW. Cipher is now developing 700 megawatts (MW) of high-performance computing capacity across three sites for hyperscaler tenants, which include Alphabet's (GOOG -2.93%) (GOOGL -3.46%) Google and Amazon (AMZN -3.87%) Web Services.

Cipher's biggest growth opportunity is expansion. Its 5.9 GW project pipeline includes the 1 GW Colchis site, which is expected to receive final approval from Texas grid regulators in December.

That said, the company isn't yet profitable, and is banking on recurring revenue from tenants to offset its big upfront infrastructure costs. Plus, with Democrats retaking the Texas governor's mansion, state house, and other statewide offices (including Attorney General and Land Commissioner) in the recent midterm elections, there are concerns that Cipher's Texas-centric strategy might no longer be an advantage.

Still, if Cipher can monetize its entire portfolio and get Colchis approved, it has a good shot of growing its current $2.7 billion market cap in the years ahead.

TeraWulf (WULF -3.50%) is in a similar position to Cipher: It's a former Bitcoin miner that has transitioned to leasing power-backed data centers. Its HPC leases now represent about 83% of the company's revenue, growing from $7.2 million in third-quarter 2025 to $63 million in Q3 2026. Meanwhile, crypto mining revenue has fallen from $43.4 million to $13.2 million during the same timeframe.

Rather than owning GPUs and leasing capacity, TeraWulf leases entire buildings to clients. Currently, its Lake Mariner data center north of Buffalo, New York, is operating at 102 MW capacity, leased to Fluidstack and Anthropic, while two more 168 MW buildings (336 MW total) are planned to be operational in first-quarter 2027. The entire campus will provide a projected $700 million of annualized lease revenue once complete.

Meanwhile, the company is building a facility in Kentucky dubbed "Justified," which has signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for roughly $19 billion. Google is providing investment-grade credit support for the project to strengthen its financing profile, and the facility has a fixed-ceiling construction contract with Fluor (FLR -3.79%). Better still for investors, TeraWulf's management says its $2.4 billion cash position will provide sufficient liquidity to fund its contracted developments without needing to issue more shares of stock.

The Anthropic deal is a major reason TeraWulf’s $6 billion market cap is so much larger than Cipher's $2.7 billion. However, a major new-tenant announcement could boost either company’s stock.

Although both Cipher and TeraWulf are in the expensive build-out phase, recent AI data center development backlash means their already-approved campuses are well-positioned for success.

It's early in the growth story for both Cipher Digital and TeraWulf, and both companies should be seen as risky bets on continued AI development. Shares are likely to remain volatile in the near term. But if AI data center investment continues to soar, both of these small companies have a better shot than Nvidia to 10x.
